paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : IWSLT14 De
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of different models in terms of BLEU score as a function of average lagging (AL), with the x-axis representing average lagging in units of tokens, ranging from 2 to 8 on a linear scale with labeled tick marks at intervals of 2. The y-axis represents the BLEU score, ranging from 20 to 32 on a linear scale with dashed gridlines at intervals of 2. Four models are compared: Consistency-CE (light purple dashed line with circle markers), Inconsistency-CE (dark purple dash-dotted line with square markers), Inconsistency-CE-MP (blue dashed line with square markers), and Consistency-Bi (red solid line with star markers). The Consistency-Bi model achieves the highest BLEU scores across all values of average lagging, starting at approximately 26.5 at AL=2 and increasing to 32 at AL=8. The Inconsistency-CE-MP model shows a similar trend, starting at approximately 23 at AL=2 and increasing to 31.5 at AL=8. The Inconsistency-CE model starts at approximately 23.5 at AL=2 and increases to 30.5 at AL=8. The Consistency-CE model starts at approximately 20.5 at AL=2 and increases to 31.5 at AL=8. All models exhibit an increasing trend in BLEU score as average lagging increases, with the Consistency-Bi model consistently outperforming the others.
